away.blurb: The veteran ball carrier exited the game in the fourth quarter as the Vikings posted 10 unanswered points to secure a 16-10 win over the visiting Colts. He was listed as questionable to return, but did not. Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones left Sunday’s win over the Indianapolis Colts with a knee injury. Fortunately for the Vikings, this injury for Jones doesn’t appear to be serious. On Monday, ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter reported a positive update on the Vikings RB. “Vikings RB Aaron Jones’ knee injury that he suffered during Sunday’s win over the Colts is not considered to be significant at this time, and a source described him as ‘day to day,'” Schefter reported. This injury for Jones occurred in the same game that fellow running back Jordan Mason returned from injured reserve. Mason missed each of the Vikings’ last four games after suffering a thumb injury in Week 1, forcing Jones to step up as the team’s bell-cow lead back. Mason led the Vikings in rushing on Sunday, taking 15 carries for 68 yards. Jones recording 26 yards on eight carries before exiting the game. The Vikings are the NFL’s last remaining undefeated team, boasting a 6-0 recording heading into this coming Sunday’s Week 8 matchup against the Detroit Lions. home.headline: Tyler Allgeier Has Fallen Behind Two Cardinals Backs, but Jahmyr Gibbs' 470-Touch Pace Could Make Him a Deadline Fit for the Lions
home.blurb: Tyler Allgeier signed with the Arizona Cardinals in March to share a backfield, and seven games later he's watching rookie Jeremiyah Love and Bam Knight take the work he was paid for. The Detroit Lions have the opposite problem. Jahmyr Gibbs is on pace for roughly 470 touches, he sat out Wednesday's practice with a shoulder injury and Bleacher Report's Kristopher Knox named Detroit the ideal landing spot for a 225-pound back Arizona no longer needs before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Arizona's line hasn't helped, and the depth chart has moved past him anyway. Knight earned the lead back job against Denver while Love was out, outsnapping Allgeier 43 to 38 in the 30-16 loss, and Love's return could bring a slot role for the rookie on top of his carries. Allgeier saw it coming as early as training camp. The Vikings will test that thinking right away. Blake Cashman earned a 94.9 PFF grade in Minnesota's 16-10 win over the Colts with two sacks and seven stops, and Brian Flores sends pressure from everywhere. If Gibbs is limited by the shoulder, or simply worn down by December, the Lions need a second back who can lower his pads on third-and-2. Allgeier hasn't shown much in Arizona, but that's the one job he's done his whole career. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his 3-week window to return from the PUP list opened this week, but he is unlikely to play on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown did not practice Wednesday with shoulder and ankle injuries, respectively, which is something to keep an eye on the rest of the week. For the Vikings, Kevin O'Connell didn't seem overly concerned about either Aaron Jones or Joe Huber. Jones is considered day-to-day while Huber sitting out practice on Wednesday was more precautionary than a sign he won't play on Sunday. Brian O'Neill continues to play through a minor knee injury. We'll see how it plays out with injury updates tomorrow and Friday. picks.blurb: 1. Klint Kubiak vowed there was "no controversy" at quarterback, where Kirk Cousins will remain the starter. While the 38-year-old might have hit a wall last week in trying to navigate the Rams ' relentless blitzes, the NFL's leading passer is hardly the Silver and Black's biggest problem. Kubiak has bemoaned an inert running game that has left Las Vegas needing to sling its way back into games. It could be tricky to get things going against a Jets defense that ranks fifth in defensive EPA per rush. 2. Can New York finally get Garrett Wilson involved early and often in the offensive game plan? One week after he was essentially a non-factor against the Patriots, Wilson was held without a reception or target in the first half against a woefully undermanned Dolphins secondary. Wilson and Glenn both downplayed the wideout's heated confrontation with quarterback Geno Smith, but expect feeding the receiver early and often to be a point of emphasis for Gang Green. 3. How the Raiders' defense handles the Jets' ground game could determine the course of the game. The Silver and Black allowed a season-high 199 rushing yards to the Rams last week, with a vulnerability that has been apparent all season finally reaching critical mass. New York, meanwhile, has seen Braelon Allen eclipse 100 rushing yards in two of the last three games he's handled as Breece Hall's fill-in. Geno Smith gets his former team, while Kirk Cousins keeps the Raiders' starting job despite the growing curiosity about Fernando Mendoza. Neither team has earned much trust lately, so let's acknowledge that before pretending this is an easy handicap. Smith threw three touchdowns against Miami, and Las Vegas' defense offers an opportunity for another productive afternoon. The Raiders need more from their running game to keep Cousins from carrying every possession. I'm giving New York the slightest edge at the Meadowlands, and a fifth straight loss for Las Vegas. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Jets 24, Raiders 20 This game could end up shaping the second half of the season for two coaching staffs that seem to be at a crossroads. The Jets' secondary might not be able to mug the Raiders' receiving corps the way that the Patriots and Rams did, but the pass rush should be able to generate sufficient heat to keep Kirk Cousins out of sorts. Las Vegas seems desperate to find any semblance of offensive balance - as well as some stops against the run - but a breakthrough might not materialize this week. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Raiders 26, Jets 20 You can put a bow on the 2026 Jets. The season, and maybe the Aaron Glenn era, came to an end with a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7. It's going to be a bumpy ride to the finish, but there is no doubt the destination is a top pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That's why it's fitting that New York will get a glimpse at what it could've had last season. Fernando Mendoza won't play, but it's the idea he's wearing silver and black that sticks. The Raiders are just better. Vegas gets back on track. Dybantsa delivers in debut Steelers underrated DB picks up new injury ahead of Week 8 vs. Browns Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire Thu, October 29, 2026 at 12:05 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers were without one of their most underrated depth contributors at Wednesday's practice ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Cleveland Browns . Courtesy of Wednesday's practice report , defensive back Doneiko Slaughter was listed as a non-participant with a hamstring injury. Slaughter was not listed on the Week 7 practice report, and it is not known when he picked up this new hamstring injury. Slaughter, who played collegiate football at Tennessee (2020–2023) and Arkansas (2024), began his NFL career as an undrafted free agent with the Jacksonville Jaguars . Slaughter would later sign a reserve/future contract with the Steelers in January 2026. He was unfortunately released during final roster cuts but subsequently signed with the Steelers' practice squad. Slaughter was elevated from the practice squad for the Steelers' first three games of the season and was signed to the active roster on October 1. He was later waived but ultimately brought back on October 10, where he now remains a vital depth contributor on the 53-man roster. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton No one predicted the Browns (5-2) would be tied for first in the AFC North heading into Week 8 of the NFL season, but here they sit as they prepare to play the Steelers (5-2) in Pittsburgh this Sunday. Cleveland has won five of its last six after beating Tennessee 27-24 last Sunday, while Pittsburgh enters on a three-game winning streak following a 16-10 victory over New Orleans in the NFL’s first regular-season game in Paris. The matchup also comes only a month after Cleveland beat Pittsburgh 27-24 on October 1. Last week, Cleveland again showed an ability to win late in their game against Tennessee. After falling behind 14-0 in the first quarter, the Browns rallied behind Quinshon Judkins , who rushed for 96 yards and two touchdowns, and rookie KC Concepcion , who caught eight passes for 129 yards. Deshaun Watson delivered perhaps his best performance of the season, completing 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards while adding a nine-yard rushing touchdown. After Tennessee tied the game with 58 seconds remaining, Watson immediately answered, hitting Harold Fannin Jr. for 36 yards to help set up Andre Szmyt’s game-winning 32-yard field goal as time expired. It was Watson’s fifth fourth-quarter winning drive of the season. Pittsburgh’s latest win was less dramatic but built around the combination it hopes can carry them to a division title and a playoff berth: Aaron Rodgers , an effective running game and a defense capable of closing out tight games. Rodgers completed 19 of 30 passes for 212 yards and a touchdown against New Orleans, including a four-yard score to Darnell Washington that gave him 540 career touchdown passes and moved him past Peyton Manning into third place in NFL history. Jaylen Warren supplied 101 rushing yards on 18 carries. The Pittsburgh defense held the Saints to just 18 rushing yards and Payton Wilson produced a red-zone interception. The biggest storyline may simply be whether Pittsburgh can reverse what happened in Cleveland four weeks earlier. In that Oct. 1 meeting, the Browns built a 21-7 advantage before Rodgers led a fourth-quarter comeback, eventually tying the game at 24 on his three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth and ensuing two-point run. Watson then went 4-for-5 for 46 yards on Cleveland’s final drive, positioning Szmyt for a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining to give the Browns a 27-24 victory. Watson finished with 268 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Rodgers threw for 299 yards and three touchdowns but was intercepted twice; DK Metcalf added 115 receiving yards and Warren ran for 93. That first meeting established the template for Sunday: division rivals comfortable playing close games led by veteran quarterbacks who have repeatedly delivered late, and a Browns team trying to complete an improbable season sweep against a Steelers club returning home looking to reclaim the upper hand in the AFC North. Let’s dive into the numbers and see if we can’t find an additional sweat or two. Cleveland ranks 27th in touchdown percentage (3.1%), 28th in points scored (19.0 per game), 30th in third-down conversion rate (32.58%), and 32nd in sack rate allowed (11.85%) with 25 sacks taken, most in the NFL. The Browns have run just 10.1% of their offensive plays in the red zone this season — worst in the NFL — and they’re averaging 8.0 drives per touchdown in the second half since 2025, worst in the league. Pittsburgh’s defense is the perfect foil. The Steelers rank 3rd in touchdown percentage allowed (2.59%), 5th in points allowed (19.71 per game), 3rd in touchdowns allowed (11), 5th in passing touchdowns allowed (1.0 per game), 7th in rushing touchdowns allowed (0.57 per game), and 6th in yards per carry allowed (3.75). He hasn't committed a penalty since Week 3. Over Cleveland's last three games, Howard has allowed zero sacks and three total pressures in 87 pass-blocking snaps, per Pro Football Focus. Jones struggled, per PFF, allowing three pressures and three hurries in his 25 offensive snaps in the game. The Browns' faith in Dawand Jones could be tested against the Steelers in Week 8 Back in training camp, head coach Todd Monken and O-line coach George Warhop talked up Jones' conditioning and upside as a veteran leader -until they didn't. In the blink of an eye , Jones flipped from getting starter's reps at left tackle to landing on the 53-man roster bubble. He made the cut as a reserve tackle, which made sense after he took a multi-million-dollar pay cut earlier in the spring, but he hasn't been replacement-level-starter material when called upon since the start of the regular season. In 60 offensive snaps, Jones has allowed one sack, six pressures, and five hurries while committing a pair of penalties, per PFF. home.headline: Steelers Named Ideal Trade Spot for 2,447-Yard AFC WR Seeking Exit
home.blurb: Aaron Rodgers has kept Pittsburgh moving despite injuries to Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson. Now, one national writer believes a receiver who reportedly wants out of his current team could be an ideal addition to the Steelers’ offense. In his Oct. 29 look at potential landing spots for available skill players, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox listed Pittsburgh as the ideal destination for Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs. Knox suggested Indianapolis could receive a high Day 3 draft selection in return. Downs is in the final year of his rookie contract, leaving any acquiring team with a decision to make about his future beyond 2026. The Pittsburgh Steelers are 5-2 and have won three straight games, but their wide receiver depth remains a concern with the NFL trade deadline approaching. Steelers Listed as Ideal Trade Landing Spot for Josh Downs Downs, 25, has reportedly asked to be moved. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday that Downs requested a trade, with other receiver-needy teams already showing interest. Knox believes Downs would make sense in Pittsburgh because of the way Rodgers has operated the offense this season. “Downs’ route-running and change-of-direction skills would fit well with the Pittsburgh Steelers’ precision-passing offense,” Knox wrote. Rodgers has often relied on quicker decisions and shorter throws rather than asking his receivers to consistently win deep. Downs, a 5-foot-9 slot target, could give him another option in those situations. The Colts selected Downs in the third round of the 2023 draft. He has 26 receptions for 307 yards without a touchdown through seven games this season. His career totals are much stronger: 224 catches for 2,447 yards and 11 touchdowns across 54 appearances. His best season came in 2024, when he caught 72 passes for 803 yards and five touchdowns. Downs added 58 catches for 566 yards and four scores last year. Josh Downs Could Address Steelers’ Growing Receiver Need The Steelers have been without Pittman since placing him on injured reserve with a foot injury Oct. 10. Wilson joined him a week later because of a finger injury, thinning the receiving corps around Rodgers. That has put more responsibility on DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard. Through seven games, Metcalf has 32 catches for 374 yards, while Bernard has 27 receptions for 254 yards. Pittsburgh beat the New Orleans Saints 16-10 on Sunday, but Rodgers threw for 212 yards and one touchdown. His longest completion was a 51-yard connection with Metcalf, a reminder of what the veteran can do when a receiver gets open downfield. Downs offers a different skill set. His ability to change direction and find space underneath would complement Metcalf rather than duplicate his role. Indianapolis has already moved two prominent veterans. away.blurb: Falcons injury report: RB Brian Robinson, LB Divine Deablo ruled out vs. 49ers Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE Atlanta has several key players who are questionable for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers. That includes the Atlanta Falcons and San Francisco 49ers, who each enter Sunday's game with availability questions for key players. Atlanta's injury report has been lengthy all week long, but it includes a few players who could be making a return in Week 7. Most notably are cornerbacks A.J. Terrell Jr. and C.J. Henderson. Their return would bolster a secondary that has been dinged up in recent weeks but was playing well at the start of the season. If Terrell, who has been on injured reserve for the last four games, and Henderson do return, that could afford a bit of flexibility in the secondary, especially with slot cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. ruled out for Sunday due to a hamstring injury he sustained late in Week 6. Bowman is one of four players ruled out against the 49ers. The others are linebacker Divine Deablo, offensive tackle Michael Jerrell and running back Brian Robinson Jr., the latter two of whom first appeared on Wednesday's injury report as limited participants with bicep and hamstring injuries, respectively. Deablo has been the key communicator for Atlanta's defense this season, but the team feels confident that rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels, who is questionable for the game with a neck injury , can step up in that area if needed. The Falcons had three players begin practicing this week after spending time on injured reserve. While those three players—wide receiver Beaux Collins, offensive lineman Cameron Williams and Terrell—are listed as questionable for the game, they would need to be added to Atlanta's active roster by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to play on Sunday. Robinson's absence was one of the more notable developments on Atlanta's final injury report. The running back was limited during Wednesday's practice before missing Thursday and Friday, ultimately being ruled out for Sunday's game. With Robinson unavailable, the Falcons will need additional contributions from their remaining running backs. away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Falcons: Initial injury report for Week 8
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their initial injury report Wednesday ahead of their Week 8 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons, with three players sitting out practice and two others participating on a limited basis. Wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, who continues to deal with concussion and foot injuries, was limited in practice. Outside linebacker Yaya Diaby was also limited due to an illness. Atlanta also opened the week with several players sidelined. Defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) and running back Brian Robinson (hamstring) did not participate in practice. Defensive end Za'Darius Smith was also held out for rest. The Falcons had six players listed as limited participants, including defensive end Samson Ebukam (hamstring), defensive linemen LaCale London (chest) and Charles Snowden (back), offensive tackle Jawaan Taylor (hamstring), cornerback Avieon Terrell (illness) and wide receiver Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). home.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
home.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. picks.headline: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8
picks.blurb: Early odds and bold Parker Washington prediction for Colts vs. Jaguars in Week 8 Skip to main content News FanSided NFL Sites Even though the Jacksonville Jaguars didn't play in Week 7, they managed to gain ground in the AFC South , as every other team in the division lost. The Jags are back from their break and will have a prime opportunity to keep building their lead when they play the hapless Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. The Colts are 2-5 and currently showing no signs of getting better this season. Heck, they let everyone know that they're punting on the season when they ousted general manager Chris Ballard, who failed to replenish the Indianapolis roster and left it devoid of talent. Following the dismissal of Ballard, Indy has gone on to hold a fire sale, sending All-Pro guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in return for a 2027 third-round pick and a fifth in 2028 days before the Jaguars game. While the Nelson trade could incentivize the Jags to make a push for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner , they cannot lose sight of the task at hand, which is beating the dreaded divisional foe. And with this in mind, here are the early odds for Week 8 and a bold Parker Washington prediction. The Colts vs. the Jaguars early odds for Week 8 The game will be held at EverBank Stadium, where the Colts have lost 11 consecutive games. Not surprisingly, the Jaguars are a 7.5-point favorite with a moneyline of -395 , via DraftKings. Bet $395 on them to win $100 if they beat Indianapolis for a total payout of $495. The Colts' moneyline sits at +310. Place a wager of $100 and win $310 if they beat Jacksonville for a total payout of $410. The over/under for the game is set at 49.5 points. ** Keep in mind that odds are refreshed periodically, so they can change at any moment. You may also like: 5 Jaguars who need to step up after the bye Bold Parker Washington prediction for the Jaguars vs. the Colts One of the biggest storylines surrounding the Jaguars in the offseason was that they opted not to make a big splash in free agency because they wanted to take care of their homegrown talent. Thus far, they locked up long snapper Ross Matiscik, defensive end Travon Walker, cornerback Montaric Brown, and tight end Brenton Strange, so you could make the case that general manager James Gladstone achieved the goal. That said, Parker Washington is still waiting on an extension. A sixth-round pick in 2023, Washington showed flashed his first two seasons but was stucked behind Christian Kirk. Jacksonville paved the way for him to start when Kirk was traded to the Houston Texans. Right off the bat, Washington became a key contributor on offense, registering 58 receptions for 807 yards with five touchdowns, all career bests, last year. Washington wasted no time picking up where he left off last year, racking up 26 receptions for 416 yards with four touchdowns. The former Penn State Nittany Lion is on pace to register the first 1,000-yard season of his career and should have no trouble getting the top-market contract he's been looking for . Although the Jags reportedly offered Washington $25 million per year before Week 1 , he rejected the offer. It's possible that he's aiming for an annual average of $30 million. Based on his production, he may be able to get it, and he'll have a prime opportunity when he plays the Colts. Already, Washington posted his first 100-yard game of the season against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. He'll get his second one in Week 8 when he registers seven receptions for a monster 140 yards with two touchdowns against Indy. away.headline: Jaguars-Colts Thursday injury report: What does Montaric Brown's return mean?
away.blurb: But what could the potential return of Brown really mean for the Jaguars in an important Week 8 AFC South battle? “Certainly, we'd have a guy who's got a lot of experience who knows our system. It'd be good to have him back out there healthy," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "I know in the Philly game, tough situation where he got hurt there in the game, but he looks good and we gain a veteran presence, and we gain a level of physicality anytime Buster's out there," Campanile said. "I think he's done a great job for us that way on the line of scrimmage, tackling, being physical, even in the coverage element of everything. So yeah, that's what we gain with him in there.” Getting Brown back at cornerback could allow the Jaguars to do a number of things differently, including getting Hunter more snaps on offense after his dominant game against the Houston Texans. Not having Brown available was the primary reason Hunter didn't play an offensive snap in Week 4 against the Bengals, which to date is the only game in Hunter's career in which he did not take a snap on both sides of the ball. Getting Brown back also happens at a good time for the secondary since safety Antonio Johnson did not practice for the second day in a row with an ankle injury. Johnson looks unlikely to play against the Colts, which means the Jaguars will need backups like Kaevon Merriweather and reinforcements like Brown to step up in the secondary. This article was originally published on www.si.com/nfl/jaguars/onsi as Jaguars-Colts Thursday Injury Report: What Does Montaric Brown's Return Mean? . JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars look like they are getting a big boost to their secondary in Week 8. The Jaguars had cornerback Montaric Brown listed as a full participant in practice for the second day in a row , a sign that Jacksonville is set to get their highest-paid cornerback back on the field against the Indianapolis Colts. Brown has missed all but six snaps over the Jaguars' last three weeks due to the hamstring injury, which first flared up on the Jaguars' injury report in the practices leading up to Week 4 against the Cincinnati Bengals. While Brown was not having a stellar season before his injury, it is worth noting that the Jaguars rank No. 28 and No. 24, respectively, in EPA/Play and success rate against the pass in the three weeks since. While Brown may not slot in as a starter right off the bat for the Jaguars, he would give them expanded depth at a critical position alongside Travis Hunter, Jarrian Jones, and Jourdan Lewis. Brown did play six snaps in Week 5 against the Philadelphia Eagles but left after allowing a long touchdown pass to Darius Cooper in man coverage, a play that clearly showed the impact of his injury. away.headline: Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report
away.blurb: In return for the All-Pro guard, the Colts received a 2027 third round pick and 2028 fifth round pick from Seattle. News Sports Things To Do Opinion Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals COLTS Quenton Nelson, Colts were close to a contract extension in the offseason, per report Cameron Cocquyt Indianapolis Star Oct. 29, 2026, 1:39 p.m. ET The Indianapolis Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks following the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Nelson had reportedly wanted to sign a long-term contract extension to remain with the Colts. In exchange for Nelson, Indianapolis received a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. After the Indianapolis Colts fired general manger Chris Ballard 10 days ago, it sent a ripple effect down the organization. Coming off a second-half letdown and loss to the then 0-5 Tennessee Titans , it seemed clear that changes were imminent. Tuesday, the Colts traded Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks , a franchise cornerstone on the offensive line since Indianapolis drafted him with the No. 6 pick in the 2018 NFL Draft . With uncertainty surrounding the future of the organization, rumors began to swirl about trade requests regarding some of the Colts' most important players. ESPN NFL insider Ian Rapoport joined the Pat McAfee show Wednesday and shed some light on Nelson's situation in Indianapolis. "Is that accurate? He wanted to get a deal done with Indianapolis this off-season," McAfee asked Rapoport. "Yeah, that is true." Rapoport replied. "When Chris Ballard was there, I really thought it was going to get done." Nelson didn't sign an extension. He is currently on the final year of a four-year, $80 million contract, his first large-scale extension following his rookie contract. According to Rapoport, it was up to Nelson if he would be spending the next several years with the Colts' organization. "This is a huge bounty for someone in the middle of the season," Rapoport added. "A lot of people wanted this guy that the Seahawks think is like really, really going to help their run game." Since arriving in Indianapolis, Nelson was selected to the Pro Bowl each of his eight seasons and was named an All-Pro in six of those. Just a short time after Nelson's trade, the Colts moved another key piece of the roster in DeForest Buckner , who returns to the organization that drafted him, the San Francisco 49ers . Indianapolis received a 2027 fourth-round pick. With uncertainty surrounding the organization, there is reason to believe the roster moves won't stop here. home.blurb: But what could the potential return of Brown really mean for the Jaguars in an important Week 8 AFC South battle? “Certainly, we'd have a guy who's got a lot of experience who knows our system. It'd be good to have him back out there healthy," Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile said on Thursday. "I know in the Philly game, tough situation where he got hurt there in the game, but he looks good and we gain a veteran presence, and we gain a level of physicality anytime Buster's out there," Campanile said. "I think he's done a great job for us that way on the line of scrimmage, tackling, being physical, even in the coverage element of everything. So yeah, that's what we gain with him in there.” Getting Brown back at cornerback could allow the Jaguars to do a number of things differently, including getting Hunter more snaps on offense after his dominant game against the Houston Texans. Not having Brown available was the primary reason Hunter didn't play an offensive snap in Week 4 against the Bengals, which to date is the only game in Hunter's career in which he did not take a snap on both sides of the ball. Getting Brown back also happens at a good time for the secondary since safety Antonio Johnson did not practice for the second day in a row with an ankle injury. Johnson looks unlikely to play against the Colts, which means the Jaguars will need backups like Kaevon Merriweather and reinforcements like Brown to step up in the secondary. Dybantsa delivers in debut Chargers vs. Rams bold predictions for NFL Week 8 Ben Strauss, ClutchPoints Thu, October 29, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The NFL teams based in Los Angeles are not having a great first half of the 2026 NFL season. Both the Chargers and Rams combined have three wins on the season headed into Week 8. The Rams are doing all of the heavy lifting here, but even they are having a disappointing season compared to their offseason expectations. It seems a Rams vs. Chargers Super Bowl is not in the cards this season. While both teams have been frustrating, they are in completely different situations ahead of Week 8. The Rams are very much alive in the NFC playoff race, but they need to continue stacking wins to remain competitive. Meanwhile, the Chargers are 0-6 and somehow still think they'll compete by the end of the season. This game means a lot for both teams, but the Rams arguably have much more to lose. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) So which team will come out on top in this one? Here are three bold predictions ahead of this Battle for Los Angeles in Week 8 between the Chargers and Rams. Rams, Chargers combine for more rushing yards than passing yards Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Both LA teams built their teams to have a strong running game. Jim Harbaugh is known for his love of pounding the rock. The Chargers drafted Omarion Hampton and built a massive offensive line for that very reason. As for the Rams, Sean McVay has always leaned heavily on the running game dating back to the Todd Gurley years. That has continued into 2026, as the Rams popularized 13 personnel usage and have taken to a new level this season. But just how committed are they to running the ball? When both teams combine their final stats, this game will feature more rushing yards than passing yards. That sounds like a crazy prediction on the surface. So exactly how bold is this prediction? The Rams average roughly 70 more passing yards than rushing yards per game this season, compared to an 82-yard gap for the Chargers. So it would be quite shocking if both teams overcame this 152-yard difference. If this happens, it may require both defenses to ball out against the pass and allow a handful of explosive runs. This is definitely bold, but crazier things have happened. The Chargers dominate the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball If the Chargers are going to have a chance to win this game, they'll have to do so in the trenches. The injury situation for both teams makes this look like a strong possibility. Joe Alt is expected to return from injury for this game. One offensive lineman won't magically turn LA's o-line into an elite unit. However, it could do wonders as he still projects as an elite talent at the position. If the Chargers can count on one side of the line protected, they can always pull out some tricks to protect the other side. It is also important to note that the Rams have only managed 10 sacks in seven games played this season. That puts them at 27th in the NFL and only ahead of pitiful defensive teams like the Dolphins, Eagles, and Cowboys. It really shows that Myles Garrett, Kobie Turner, and Poona Ford are injured. Flipping to the other side, the Chargers and Rams look pretty evenly matched in the trenches. The Rams may hold a slight lead, but nothing too crazy. Ultimately, the Chargers' formula for winning this game is predicated on winning the trenches. This is certainly an area where they could gain an advantage. The Chargers will keep Justin Herbert completely clean, not allowing a single sack. Meanwhile, they will sack Matthew Stafford at least twice. That may not be a huge advantage, but it gives the Chargers a fighting chance. Chargers take Rams to overtime, but lose by a field goal Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images It is really tempting to predict that the Chargers will get their first win of the season in this spot. But it just seems too far-fetched. Realistically, the Rams and Chargers are in two completely different worlds on offense. The Rams average more total yards per game than any other team, while the Chargers are statistically a bottom five offense. There's no reason to suggest that will change in Week 8. Furthermore, the Rams absolutely must win this game to stay alive in the NFC playoff race. McVay may be willing to pull out all the stops if this game becomes close, and the Chargers would need to be lucky to survive in that situation. But playing for pride is important too, so the Chargers won't go down without a fight. They just don't have the horses to get the job done. Brandon McManus kicks a game-winning field goal in overtime, cementing himself as the Rams' kicker for the rest of the season. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Chargers are set to take on the Rams this Sunday in their seventh game of the season, though Derwin James Jr. may be out. James could be entering the injured reserve after suffering a setback in his return from hamstring injury. With James out, Elijah Molden, Tony Jefferson, and Genesis Smith have picked up the slack. While the Chargers remain the only winless team in the NFL, their defense has been a bright spot. James would be the latest of their star players to hit the IR. If the Chargers decide to go down that route, he will be eligible to return for their Week 12 game against the Patriots. The 30-year-old safety has been held to three games this season, and has not played in the entire month of October. The Chargers can’t seem to catch a break. They’ve been hit with a slew of injuries on both sides of the ball, including some of their best players. In the season, James has 21 tackles and one passes defended in what has been a tough season for the team. Ealier in the season, James suffered a pinky injury; however, he played through it while wearing a cast. At this point, it appears unlikely that James will be able to suit up on Sunday. home.headline: Rams star Matthew Stafford's wife Kelly hits out at NFL over head injuries after bombshell new study
home.blurb: Kelly Stafford, the wife of Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, took aim at the NFL over the safety of playing conditions on Thursday. Kelly, who has been married to the reigning MVP since 2015, called on the NFL to ban turf at stadiums around the league amid rising concerns over brain trauma injuries among players. A new study published this week found that 75 percent of former NFL players who died between 2008 and 2023 had the neurodegenerative brain disease known as chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE. Following the bombshell news, Kelly took to her Instagram stories to criticize the NFL for its lack of action over player safety. 'GET RID OF TURF. PLEASE. / Will it fix everything? No. Will it eliminate injuries? Absolutely not. But my goodness, wouldn't it be a step in the right direction?' the mother-of-four's caption read. 'You want your "stars" to last in this league? The guys who bring in the viewers, fill the stadiums, sell the jerseys, and make this league billions? Then why aren't we doing EVERYTHING we can to protect them? / We know there are serious concerns about turf and the injuries that come with playing on it. Knees, ankles, ligaments… you name it. / But what really gets me is the HEAD,' she continued. 'Listen, I know what sport my husband plays. I know what these men signed up for. Football is physical. It's violent. Heads are going to collide. Bodies are going to hit the ground. That part of the game isn't going away…' Kelly followed up her message with another post that read: 'But here's the thing… / We can't always control what these players hit. But we sure as hell can control what they land on. / And if there's a chance that changing the surface beneath them could reduce even ONE serious injury, shouldn't we be doing everything possible to make that happen?' She claimed that football players grapple with the toll the game takes on their bodies long after the final whistle, as she urged the league to consider the young generation watching the game and aspiring to one day join the ranks of the NFL. 'I've watched what this game takes from these men,' she added. 'I've seen the injuries, the surgeries, the pain they play through, and the toll it can take on their head long after the final whistle. / And I love this game. Our family loves this game. That's exactly WHY I want it to be better. 'Because this isn't just about the NFL. It's about the kids watching. The kids dreaming of playing on Sundays. The colleges, the high schools, the youth leagues that look to the NFL to set the standard. / So SET IT. 'You have the money. You have the resources. You have the ability to lead the way. / No, grass isn't going to solve every problem. But doing nothing because we can't fix everything? That's not good enough. @nfl.' Kelly's husband Stafford, with whom she shares four daughters, has played 18 seasons in the NFL, winning the Super Bowl in 2022. Dybantsa delivers in debut Frank Schwab Senior writer Thu, October 29, 2026 at 3:49 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the Denver Broncos, Week 1 had to feel like a bad flashback. The first 12 times that Patrick Mahomes started against the Broncos, the Kansas City Chiefs won every time. Then there was a shift with Sean Payton in charge, and the Broncos won two of three against Mahomes and the Chiefs. The 2026 season opener, though, was like old times. It wasn't Mahomes that ruined the Broncos in the opener, though he played pretty well. It was Kenneth Walker III doing most of the damage, as he ran through many Denver missed tackles for 173 rushing yards. Also, the Chiefs' defense shut down Denver in a 31-10 win. It was a complete, impressive performance. It doesn't seem like much has changed since then. The Chiefs started 5-0 before losing last week at Seattle, a very tough opponent. The Broncos are 5-2 but questions persist about their offense. While the defense on the whole has been better for the Broncos, the run defense isn't great. Denver is 26th in EPA ( expected points added ) per rush allowed. It's easy to say that the Seahawks showed everyone how to beat the Chiefs — take Walker out of the game — but not everyone has Seattle's defense to pull that off. The Broncos showed once they aren't a great matchup against Walker. That's a big reason Kansas City -1.5 is the pick. We saw in the season opener that the Chiefs' dominance over the Broncos might not be over. Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III had 173 rushing yards in Week 1 against the Broncos. (AP Photo/Colin E. Braley) Here are the rest of the picks against the spread for Week 8 of the NFL season: Panthers (+3.5) over Packers There's no way the Panthers are as bad as they played last week, when they were down 33-6 to the Buccaneers by halftime. Competent teams that get embarrassed usually bounce back well. The Packers are still a tough team to predict. Raiders (+1.5) over Jets The early East Coast start has been death for the Raiders for a long time, but they are probably the better team. They are certainly the better coached team. The Raiders are on a four-game losing streak but look at the opponents: Chiefs, Patriots, Bills, Rams. Those are four of the strongest teams in the NFL. If Las Vegas can't win here, it might be Fernando Mendoza time. Cowboys (-6.5) over Cardinals The Cowboys are going to score. The Cardinals have given up at least 30 points in six of their eight games. Dallas showed on Monday night that its offense is back, but what about the defense? Maybe a strong fourth quarter against the Eagles is a sign that the Cowboys' defense can be somewhat competent. It's scary to pick the Dallas laying points to anyone because they'll need to get stops, but it would be a surprise if they don't score 30. Buccaneers (-2.5) over Falcons Good luck figuring out either of these teams. The Buccaneers could be better than we think. Their only significant weakness has been pass offense, and that is explained by having an undrafted rookie starting three of their seven games. We don't know if Baker Mayfield is fully healthy, considering he had just 11 pass attempts in his return from a dislocated right thumb last week, but if he is maybe the Bucs can get on a roll. Browns (+3.5) over Steelers Teams coming back from an international game and playing right away without a bye are 0-3-1 this season. The losses were by 12, 11, and 6 points, and the close loss was by the Texans as a 10-point favorite last week. The tie was the Commanders when they were favored at home against the Giants. It's a hard turnaround, and it's what the Steelers face coming back from Paris last Sunday. Both of these teams are 5-2 but flawed, and I'll ride with the angle of the Browns not being the team that played in France last week. Jaguars (-9.5) over Colts It's hard to imagine being a Colts player this week. Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded and everyone else with any value has to wonder if they're next. It's actually surprising the line is less than 10 points against a Jaguars team coming off a bye and a loss. This one could get really ugly. The remainder of the Colts' season could get really ugly. Ravens (+3.5) over Bills You've seen this here before: This all depends on if Lamar Jackson plays. This week, I assume he will. It seemed like he was close last week and he practiced in full on Wednesday. There would be some real frustration if he's not back for this game, which Baltimore might need to win to start to save its season. The Ravens' remaining schedule is the toughest in the NFL, according to DVOA . If he does play, we know the Bills defense is not very good. Getting more than a field goal seems good. Vikings (+3.5) over Lions If the Vikings' build was reversed, and they had a fun offense that was clearly one of the two best in the sport but a defense that was unreliable and among the 10 worst in the NFL, we'd respect them more. How do we know that? The 2026 Buffalo Bills, that's how. Minnesota's defense has been remarkable. Look at the Chicago Bears this season. In three of Caleb Williams' four starts, Chicago is averaging 39 points. In the other start, against the Vikings, the Bears scored three points at home (Williams got injured in that game but not until the middle of the fourth quarter). Maybe Detroit will figure out Brian Flores' defense, but nobody else has and I'm willing to take more than a field goal with the Vikings. Titans (+10.5) over Bengals The Titans have been blown out only twice. They lost by 13 to the Jets in Week 1 and 23 to the Texans in Week 5. Every other game has been decided by six or fewer points. The Titans have won only one of those games, but they're keeping it close. It's possible Joe Burrow will add to his growing MVP argument and torch Tennessee in a blowout, but this seems like a good spot for an ugly underdog. Rams (-6.5) over Chargers Typically, an 0-6 team coming off a bye would be a fine choice. The Chargers don't want to get embarrassed all season, but they're simply not a good team in any phase. That is shocking but also irrefutable. This is the exact type of contrarian pick I'd like to make but I just can't get there with the Chargers. Patriots (-7) over Dolphins It's possible the Dolphins get some confidence from their first win. It's also possible they let down a bit: It's still a 1-5 team whose goal was to get that first win out of the way. On the other side, there's a Patriots team coming off a loss with three extra days of rest. Commanders (-5.5) over Eagles A low point of this week was looking at the schedule and realizing this was the Sunday night game. Not fun. Not sure what's more surprising: That a 1-4-1 Commanders team is a 5.5-point favorite over the Eagles, or that the Commanders are the pick. The Eagles' best remaining effort was going to come on a Monday night against the rival Cowboys, and that effort was pretty meager. It won't get better. Not that anyone in Broncos Country needs a reminder. Denver was flogged 31-10 by the Kansas City Chiefs. And the Broncos defense still hasn't tackled Kenneth Walker. Thankfully, and hopefully, Denver gets a crack at a redo this Sunday in Denver. A win at home against Patrick Mahomes, Walker, and Kansas City would give the Broncos the lead in the AFC West. FanDuel Sportsbook has Denver as the home underdog at +1.5 points, though that's basically a pick 'em at this point. The total sits over/under 40.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Force Mahomes into some rushed throws and/or punch the ball out to give Bo Nix and the offense some added possessions. On top of that, Nix and the offense need to continue to protect the ball. Dybantsa delivers in debut Chiefs vs. Broncos Preview: AFC West Rivals Prepare for Crucial Showdown Photo by: Joe Camporeale Stephan Stroud Thu, October 29, 2026 at 8:28 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs will travel to Denver on Sunday for a crucial AFC West matchup against the Broncos. With Kansas City sitting at 5-1 and Denver at 5-2, both teams have plenty at stake as they look to strengthen their position in the division race. The game is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET at Empower Field at Mile High and will air on CBS. The Broncos enter with momentum after winning three consecutive games, while the Chiefs are looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season. Chiefs Look to Bounce Back Head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes will try to get Kansas City back on track after a disappointing 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. The Chiefs struggled to generate offense, finishing with just 213 total yards and failing to reach the red zone. Mahomes threw for 165 yards and an interception in the defeat. He will need a stronger performance against a Denver defense that has consistently pressured opposing quarterbacks this season. Running back Kenneth Walker III could be a major factor after dominating the Broncos in the teams' first meeting. Walker rushed for 173 yards and a touchdown in Kansas City's 31-10 victory in September. If the Chiefs can establish their ground game again, it could open opportunities for Mahomes and the passing attack. Broncos Aim to Protect Home Field Denver head coach Sean Payton will look to keep his team's winning streak alive behind quarterback Bo Nix. The second-year quarterback has shown his ability to make plays with both his arm and legs, and he delivered an impressive performance in the Broncos' 30-16 win over Arizona. Nix threw for 222 yards and added 73 rushing yards, including a 62 yard touchdown run. His mobility could be important against a Kansas City defense that will try to disrupt Denver's offensive rhythm. The Broncos' defense will also be key. Led by pass rushers Nik Bonitto and Zach Allen, Denver has the ability to pressure Mahomes and force mistakes. Cornerback Pat Surtain II's improved injury status could provide a boost to the secondary, although Denver's final injury report will be worth monitoring. What to Watch For The biggest matchup will be Kansas City's offense against Denver's pass rush. If the Broncos consistently pressure Mahomes, they could make life difficult for the Chiefs. However, Kansas City's experience and offensive talent make the visitors dangerous in any close game.

picks.blurb: 1. With Kenneth Walker III coming to town, the Broncos will be called on to clean up an operation that missed 28 tackles in the Chiefs' season-opening romp. Kansas City surely wants to get the Super Bowl 60 MVP back to his early-season form after the Seahawks kept him in check. Denver has shown signs in recent weeks of its run defense coalescing, but Sunday will mark a stiff test after the group overwhelmed shorthanded backfields in the last two weeks. 2. Injuries loom large in the matchup between the Chiefs' aerial attack and the Broncos' vaunted pass defense. Getting receiver Rashee Rice and right tackle Jaylon Moore back could provide a significant boost to a Kansas City attack coming off arguably the worst offensive outing of Patrick Mahomes' tenure. But Denver could also get significant reinforcements with cornerback Patrick Surtain II trying to play after sitting out three weeks with an ankle injury. 3. A methodical Denver offense finally found its explosive streak last week against Arizona, with Bo Nix and RJ Harvey both reeling off long touchdowns. Repeating that effort against the Chiefs could be difficult, especially with Jaylen Waddle's status in question after he suffered a chest injury late against Arizona. But the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, who had 93 rushing yards in his first game back from injured reserve, could help the Broncos avoid the obvious passing situations that plagued the team early in the season. (5-2). Kansas City is coming off its first loss of the season, while Denver has won three straight and can move ahead of the Chiefs in the division with a victory. The teams met in the season opener on September 14 at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs rolled to a 31-10 win, outgaining Denver 392 yards – 176 yards. Patrick Mahomes threw two touchdown passes and ran for another score, but the star of the night was offseason addition Kenneth Walker III who gashed Denver for 173 rushing yards and a touchdown on 23 carries. The Chiefs arrive in Denver looking to rebound from their 20-3 loss at Seattle last weekend, a game in which they were simply outclassed as Mahomes and co. never found a rhythm. Kansas City managed only 213 total yards and 11 first downs and failed to reach the red zone, while Mahomes completed 19 of 33 passes for 165 yards with no touchdowns and an interception. Walker, facing his former team, was held to just 36 yards on 14 carries after entering the night averaging a league-leading 133 rushing yards per game. Seattle controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes, converted 11 of 16 third downs and got 150 receiving yards and a touchdown from Jaxon Smith-Njigba . Even when Kansas City had chances to get back into the game, Harrison Butker missed field goals from 58 and 45 yards, leaving the Chiefs with only a third-quarter field goal. Denver, meanwhile, enters with momentum after a 30-16 road win over Arizona. Bo Nix supplied the game’s biggest play with a career-long 62-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter and finished with 222 passing yards and 73 rushing yards, while RJ Harvey turned a screen pass into a 52-yard touchdown and J.K. Dobbins added a one-yard score. The Broncos’ defense repeatedly disrupted Jacoby Brissette and the Cardinals’ offense, producing 12 quarterback hits, six tackles for loss and three sacks. Kansas City owns a 74-59 all-time advantage and dominated Denver with a 16-game winning streak from 2015 through 2023, including Mahomes winning his first 12 starts against the Broncos. away.blurb: The Denver Broncos received a bit of good news and a bit of bad news today. The good news is that both wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and defensive lineman Zach Allen were back practicing. They were both held out with injuries suffered on Sunday in the win over the Arizona Cardinals. away.headline: Kansas City Chiefs Cornerback Mansoor Delane's Week 8 Status in Question
away.blurb: Kansas City Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane has played well in his first five professional games. He has 27 total tackles, one interception and five pass defenses. He stood out in the Sept. 27 and Oct. 4 games against the Miami Dolphins and Las Vegas Raiders with 10 tackles in each game. Delane missed practice Thursday with a shoulder injury. Delane had a shoulder injury in training camp that led into the preseason and cost him valuable weeks of repetitions. He aggravated that injury in Week 1 when he picked off a pass by Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix, and it forced him to miss the Week 2 game. He wasn’t listed on the team’s injury report Wednesday , which means this isn’t likely a maintenance day. It also puts his Week 8 status in question in an important game against the reigning AFC West-champion Broncos. Delane has a 79.7 PFF grade , which rates him seventh among 103 eligible cornerbacks. His PFF coverage grade of 77.4 ranks ninth, and his run-defense grade of 81.6 ranks ninth at the position. If Delane is unable to go, the Chiefs could go with a rotation of nickel corner L’Jarius Sneed and Kristian Fulton. Sneed is also dealing with a knee ailment. Friday will be a big day in determining who will be deployed in the secondary Sunday afternoon.

away.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have listed five players on their injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks . Chiefs rule out players as others remain questionable According to the Kansas City Chiefs , five players are listed on the injury report ahead of Sunday Night Football against the Seattle Seahawks. L'Jarius Sneed and Cooper McDonald are questionable, while Rashee Rice, Jaylon Moore and Brashard Smith are out. Left tackle Josh Simmons was previously placed on injured reserve with a back injury . Sneed and McDonald are both dealing with knee injuries. Sneed was limited in practice throughout the week, leaving his availability for the game against Seattle uncertain. McDonald is also listed as questionable because of his knee injury. He was designated to return from injured reserve on October 20 and has participated in limited practices since then. Moore has been ruled out because of a concussion. The offensive tackle missed practice while dealing with the injury, creating an opening along the offensive line. Joshua Ezeudu is a possible replacement at right tackle. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has practiced fully and does not carry an injury designation for the game. Rice, Moore and Smith have been ruled out, while Sneed and McDonald are listed as questionable. home.source: Denver Broncos On SI on MSN
home.blurb: Denver listed wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (chest), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), and defensive end Zach Allen (hip) — all starters — as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) following Wednesday's session. Hufanga remains on the wrong side of questionable after missing the last two games due to an ankle injury. The former AFC Defensive Player of the Week will need to get in at least limited practices on Thursday and Friday to have a shot at suiting up versus Kansas City. Allen's apparently hamstring ailment is a new development, though one that, as of this writing, seems unlikely to hold him out of Week 8 action. Elsewhere on the injury report, left tackle Garett Bolles (hip) and wide receiver Marvin Mims (ankle) were considered limited, while cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle), defensive tackle Malcolm Roach (neck), and inside linebacker Karene Reid (elbow) were full participants. Surtain appears poised to return from a three-game absence as his ankle presumably is at or near full health. Of note on the Chiefs' end, cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (personal/knee) did not practice on Wednesday while receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) and tight end Travis Kelce (ankle) were full goes. “I think to his credit, whenever we ask something of him—whether it’s intermediate, down the field—he’s been really effective," he said of Mims on Wednesday. "Obviously as a returner, that first return with the ball midfield, those are... I’ve said this before, the receiving now to start the game. [At] minimum there’s a threshold, but to start where we started, those are things that he’s shown us consistently. He continues to have those touches and then where you want to even get him more touches. It’s sometimes a challenge, but certainly he’s deserving.” The Denver Broncos released their initial Week 8 injury report ahead of Sunday's pivotal home showdown against the Kansas City Chiefs. An earlier report indicated that Waddle suffered a re-aggravation of a prior chest issue toward the end of last week's victory over the Arizona Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game is to be determined. The injury occurred on a trick play that head coach and offensive playcaller Sean Payton consequently apologized for. "Why didn't anybody ask me about the dumb reverse call? ... It was awful. I'm sorry," Payton said in his postgame press conference on Sunday. "If you look it up, in 2008, in a similar situation — even a more radical reverse — fumbled, Tampa Bay beat us. I know better. Every once in a while you fall in love with a play." Contingency Plan Must be Established In the event that Waddle is inactive on Sunday, the Broncos would be down to Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims, and Troy Franklin as its primary wideouts, with Pat Bryant (ankle) still on short-term injured reserve. Dolphins (1-5) team that earned its first win of the season last week. The Patriots average 22.9 points per game compared with Miami’s 16.3. New England’s three-game winning streak ended in a 30-24 loss at Chicago last Thursday, despite Drake Maye completing 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards and two touchdowns while also rushing for a score. The loss can be attributed to a costly interception from Maye in the red zone in the second quarter and New England compounded it with 10 penalties and a defense that missed 16 tackles. Miami, meanwhile, is coming off its best afternoon of the season, a 28-25 road victory over the Jets on October 25 that gave coach Jeff Hafley his first win and kept the Dolphins from starting 0-6. Malik Willis was the catalyst, completing 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns to rookie Caleb Douglas , adding 37 rushing yards and another score, and converting a game-clinching fourth-and-1 in the final two minutes. Miami scored touchdowns on three of its first four possessions and led 21-7 at halftime before a late Jets comeback made things interesting. Ollie Gordon II rushed for 103 yards and a touchdown, while Douglas’ 63-yard fourth-quarter catch-and-run provided the winning points. This rivalry has swung toward New England recently after several seasons in which Miami consistently gave the Patriots problems. The teams’ most recent meeting came January 4, 2026, when New England completed a season sweep with a dominant 38-10 victory at Gillette Stadium to finish the 2025 regular season 14-3. Rhamondre Stevenson was the centerpiece, rushing seven times for 131 yards and two touchdowns and catching another touchdown from Maye, while TreVeyon Henderson added two rushing scores; Maye finished 14 of 18 for 191 yards and a touchdown before exiting early in the fourth quarter. New England outgained Miami 457-180. That capped the Patriots’ first season sweep of Miami since 2016. away.blurb: Brown was limited in both practices before the Thursday night game in Chicago and still played 90.7 percent of the offensive snaps in a 30-24 loss. He also missed a couple of blocks that night, which he addressed directly. Six catches on 16 targets over two games is a thin return so far on the first-round pick and change the Patriots spent to acquire him, and Brown admitted in the same session that his explosiveness has come and gone. Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins are both on injured reserve. Hollins is eligible to return next week, while Doubs cannot come back until Week 12 . Without Brown, Drake Maye would lean on DeMario Douglas and Kyle Williams, who each caught a touchdown of 34 yards or longer against the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 11, plus tight ends Hunter Henry and Eli Raridon. Raridon scored from 30 yards out in Chicago. The New England Patriots got more injury news on A.J. Brown on Thursday ahead of Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium, with two of their receivers already on injured reserve. Brown was not practicing Thursday because of a "knee issue that has flared up," NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported, citing sources. ESPN's Mike Reiss also noted that Brown was absent from the portion of practice open to the media. "Brown also was listed on yesterday's injury report with an ankle. Knee was added, as well, and his status for Sunday is up in the air," Rapoport wrote. The ankle dates back to the season opener against the Seattle Seahawks , when Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve. New England went 3-1 during the four games he missed. He came back against the New York Jets and then played at the Chicago Bears , two games in five days, catching six of his 16 targets for 75 yards. Have the Patriots been asking too much of A.J. Brown? "I won't make any excuses," Brown told reporters. A player still getting treatment on a high-ankle sprain who carries a near-full snap load days after his first game back, then lands on the report with a second joint, gives New England's staff plenty to weigh before Sunday. What the Patriots have at receiver if A.J. Brown sits The Patriots are 4-3 and second in the AFC East, and Miami sits last in the division at 1-5. Against that opponent, with Hollins close to returning, one week off costs New England far less than another game at nearly every snap on a sore knee and ankle. away.headline: A.J. Brown injury update: Patriots wide receiver misses more practice
away.blurb: Brown did not practice with the rest of his team on Thursday, Oct. 29, according to multiple reports. The star wide receiver was already limited in practice on Wednesday, Oct. 28 with a couple of lower body injuries, but his practice status has regressed as the week has progressed. The former Philadelphia Eagles wideout has already missed four games this season after a high ankle sprain in Week 1 landed him on injured reserve . Brown has played in three out of the Patriots ' seven games since New England sent a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick to Philadelphia to acquire the receiver . The 29-year-old Brown did not practice on Oct. 29 as he deals with injuries to his ankle and knee. NFL Media and ESPN insider Ian Rapoport reported on Oct. 29 that the Patriots initially listed Brown on their injury report on Oct. 28 as a limited participant with a knee injury. The team has since added an ailing ankle to the receiver's injury designation as he misses practice for the first time since his Week 6 return. That is a notably short list of healthy receivers – and Brown may not be healthy. New England already has the other two of its top three receivers out on injured reserve: Romeo Doubs with a shoulder and Mack Hollins with a calf. The Patriots do have four more wide receivers on their practice squad to fill out their depth, especially if Brown is unable to play in Week 8: Ryan Miller, Cameron Dorner, Kyle Dixon and Chandler Brayboy. Here's what we know about the three-time Pro Bowler's status: Brown has appeared to be less than 100% recovered in his first two games back off of injured reserve. The wideout made his comeback in Week 6 against the Jets, where he promptly dropped two of his 10 targets and finished the game with just three catches. In Week 7 against the Bears, Brown caught three of his six targets but was 0-for-2 on contested targets and tallied just one yard after the catch, per Pro Football Focus. Brown's status for Week 8 remains unknown. Here's how things would look in the Patriots' receivers room if Brown is able to go on Sunday, Nov. 1: Miller is in his fourth season and appeared in five games for the Dolphins this year before they waived him. Dorner and Dixon are both UDFA rookies. Brayboy is a second-year receiver yet to make his NFL debut.

home.headline: Thursday Injury Update: Big Names Could Be Missing from Dolphins-Patriots Matchup
home.blurb: Based on the NFL's five-step Return to Play protocol, Proctor still has to go through "non-contact training drills" and then "full football activity involving contact." The final injury report will come out Friday and at this time it would be a surprise if Proctor weren't ruled out. After being limited in practice because of an ankle injury Wednesday, Brown sat out Thursday and now also is dealing with a knee issue. After sitting out practice Wednesday, he was back at practice Thursday, albeit on a limited basis. The injury report again eight other players listed as limited participants. The other five players listed as limited were TE Greg Dulcich (ankle), S Michael Taaffe (neck/foot), S Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder), WR Malik Washington (knee) and WR Jared Wayne (knee). Besides Brown, the one change on the Patriots injury report involved running back TreVeyon Henderson, who did not practice Thursday because of illness. Henderson, a second-year second-round pick out of Ohio State, has had a slow start to his 2026 seaosn as the backfield partner to Rhamondre Stevenson, but he did score two touchdowns against Miami in the 2025 season finale. Starting right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) against was limited, while QB Drake Maye was listed with a right shoulder injury, but he was a full participant. The Miami Dolphins look like they're going to be without their top rookie draft pick when they try to upset the New England Patriots on Sunday, but they also might not have to face New England's prized offseason acquisition. Starting with the Dolphins, guard Kadyn Proctor missed a second consecutive practice with a concussion, and it's very difficult to envision him getting clearance to play Sunday. With the Dolphins down to one practice before a walk-through Saturday, it's again difficult to envision Proctor getting clearance in time and also know that the team is going to err on the side of caution here. Head coach Jeff Hafley indicated Wednesday that backup Jarrett Kingston would be taking Proctor's reps at left guard during practice. Kingston was the one who replaced Jonah Savaiinaea at right guard after the 2025 second-round pick was injured in the first half of the Week 5 loss at Hard Rock Stadium. Kingston, who obviously is the No. 3 guard on the roster, was claimed off waivers from the Houston Texans after the cuts to 53. picks.blurb: 1. Philadelphia needs a reset: The Eagles have dropped five straight after a 2-0 start, with Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys moving them to 2-5. Another division loss would make an already difficult climb even steeper for a team that's more realistically already on to 2027 due to so many key injuries. 2. Keep an eye on Saquon: Speaking of injuries, Saquon Barkley played only nine snaps Monday while dealing with hamstring and back issues. He offered an encouraging assessment of his hamstring and said he doesn't expect the back problem to keep him out. His practice workload still warrants watching. 3. The preparation advantage favors Washington: The Commanders come off their bye, while the Eagles turn around from Monday night for a Sunday road game. That's valuable extra time to prepare for Tanner McKee and the Eagles' reshuffled offense. 4. McKee needs help from his defense: Philadelphia's quarterback threw for 211 yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. The Eagles produced three touchdown drives, but their defense couldn't slow the Cowboys. Sustaining drives only helps so much if the other team keeps answering. 5. We should expect points: With a game total around 40.5, we're not asking for much to hit 41 points, even from these two offenses. The trends are on our side. Commanders coach Dan Quinn is 8-1 to the over in division games since the start of last season, while the Eagles are 7-1 to the over against the Commanders under coach Nick Sirianni. Commanders vs Eagles odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Eagles -1.5 Moneyline: Eagles -125; Commanders +105 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Commanders vs Eagles USA TODAY expert picks Adam Kaufman: Commanders 24, Eagles 17 Philadelphia showed some offensive life Monday, but the injury situation keeps getting in the way. Saquon Barkley aggravated his hamstring and played only nine snaps, leaving another major question around an offense already operating without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee can keep things functional when the Eagles protect him and stay balanced. That becomes much harder if the Commanders take away the run and force longer passing situations. Washington also has the benefit of a bye and lots of extra rest, while Philadelphia turns around from Monday night. It's so disappointing this is a primetime game. Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz: Eagles 19, Commanders 14 Seldom has prime time featured two teams facing such desperation around midseason. The severely shorthanded Eagles offense finally showed signs of life against the Cowboys, though the once-reliable defense suffered perhaps its worst performance of the Vic Fangio era. Expect a bounce-back outing against a Washington team short on weapons. Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Commanders 23, Eagles 13 The Commanders haven't won a game that Jayden Daniels started in since Oct. 5, 2025. Washington is 0-7-1 in the eight starts after that victory, but the time has come as the team comes out of the bye. They have run out of alarms to describe the fire on Dan Quinn's seat, making this contest a must-win for the Commanders to have any chance of making the playoffs in a weak NFC East. Against a battered and bruised Eagles squad that is running out of players, there is no better time for Washington to get back in the win column. away.headline: Eagles make Jalen Carter mistake on practice injury report
away.blurb: The Eagles already have a stacked injury report going into Week 8, with stars such as running back Saquon Barkley and wide receiver DeVonta Smith missing multiple games over the past few weeks. But on Thursday, Philadelphia initially added Carter to the injury report, listing him as a limited participant with an abdominal injury. Fortunately for the Eagles faithful, the addition of Carter to the injury report turned out to be a mistake, and the defensive tackle remains healthy going into Week 8. To fix the error, Philadelphia removed Carter from the injury report and added defensive back Michael Carter II, who is actually dealing with an abdominal issue. Along with Carter II, other notable Eagles players limited in practice on Thursday was safety Marcus Epps (jaw/concussion), defensive tackle Moro Ojomo (neck) and linebacker Nolan Smith Jr. (concussion). Jalen Carter and the Philadelphia Eagles suffered a fifth straight loss during Week 7’s edition of “Monday Night Football,” falling to 2-5 on the 2026 NFL season after a 38-21 loss to Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys. Heading into Week 8, the Eagles now look to get back on track despite a heavy injury report, hitting the road to face Jayden Daniels and the Washington Commanders. Despite the poor start to 2026 for Philadelphia, Carter is on track to have the best statistical season of his four-year NFL career. Through seven games, the former Georgia Bulldogs defensive tackle has totaled 18 tackles, three sacks, two pass deflections and a career-high three forced fumbles. But ahead of the matchup against Washington, Philadelphia made an error on the injury report that may have scared some fans momentarily. “Update: No injury for Jalen Carter. Michael Carter has an abdomen injury,” The Athletic’s Zach Berman wrote on X. Carter and the Eagles will face the Commanders in Week 8’s edition of “Sunday Night Football” at 8:20 p.m. ET. home.headline: Former Washington coach on how Commanders could replace Terry McLaurin
home.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
home.blurb: “I think Treylon Burks is probably the guy,” Gruden told “Grant and Danny” of 106.7 The Fan. “They want more from Stefon Diggs. He’s getting a little bit older. I think his snap count should be around 35 to 40 a game and Antonio’s a guy that’s got to step up. He’s a rookie, and he’s probably talent-wise, he can do a little bit of everything. I’m interested to see how he does. Dyami Brown, who knows? Maybe he’ll get some opportunities too. But, do it by, you know, committee. You don’t have to have one guy do it. There’s been a lot of teams out there that have been successful that spread the ball around. Let all of them get a few touches. Let this Chig guy make some plays at the tight end. Let Rachaad White make some plays out of the backfield or Austin Ekeler or whoever it might be. You got to spread the ball around, and then Jayden can use his legs some. So, by committee, that’s the way they got to do it.” The loss of Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin left a gaping hole on their roster. Former Commanders head coach Jay Gruden weighed in on who he believed would step up in his absence, including Treylon Burks and rookie Antonio Williams. Burks seems like someone who could really step up. He was a former first-round pick for the Tennessee Titans and has shown flashes throughout his NFL career, including his touchdown grab in Washington’s lone win of the season against the Seattle Seahawks. Burks also had a season-high in targets (six), receptions (four) and receiving yards (66) in their last game against the San Francisco 49ers. Williams has also flashed at times and scored a touchdown in the season opener against the Philadelphia Eagles. Tight end Chig Okonkwo missed some time due to injury, but has been a key part of Washington’s receiving game the past three weeks. The Commanders may not typically run a committee system, but it could work for them for the rest of the season with the talent they have. It also would not be surprising to see them trade for a receiver before the deadline.
