Barkley's status remains one of the biggest concerns after the veteran suffered a back injury during Monday night's 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. The Eagles listed him with hamstring and back injuries Wednesday, adding another concern for a player who recently returned from a hamstring issue that kept him out of consecutive games. Barkley opened the Dallas matchup with a 29-yard run and scored a touchdown on Philadelphia's first possession, but his workload was limited after his back tightened. He eventually left the game, forcing the Eagles to rely on their remaining running backs. Lemon responded with his first career touchdown reception against the Cowboys, but the Eagles would benefit from having additional receiving options available against Washington. Campbell was listed as a nonparticipant with hamstring and quadriceps injuries, adding to concerns for a defense that struggled against Dallas. Jones was sidelined by a hamstring injury, while Covey was listed with a knee injury after leaving Monday night's game. The defensive injury situation extends beyond those six players. Outside linebackers Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith were all listed as limited participants, along with defensive backs Michael Carter II, linebacker Smael Mondon Jr. and defensive tackle Moro Ojomo. The Eagles return to practice Thursday, and actual participation should better indicate which players are progressing toward Sunday's game. The injury comes at a difficult time for Philadelphia, which has lost five straight games and struggled to produce consistently on offense. The Chicago Bears and Caleb Williams are 5-2 and riding high off a primetime win in Week 7, but now they’ll have to go on the road to take on the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 8. Seattle also won in primetime in Week 7, holding the Kansas City Chiefs to just three points on Sunday Night Football to get back over .500 this season (4-3). These two teams are both in second place in their respective divisions, and this game could have massive wild card implications in the NFC. The NFC North currently has four teams over .500 while the NFC West has two with the 3-4 Los Angeles Rams lurking as a viable Super Bowl contender if they can get healthy. Oddsmakers have set the Seahawks as favorites in this game, and the opening odds tell us that they could end up being more than field-goal favorite by the time this game kicks off. Bears vs. Seahawks Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bears +3 (-102) Seahawks -3 (-118) Seahawks: -170 46.5 (Over -110/Under -110) Based on these odds (-170 on the moneyline), the Seahawks have an implied probability of 62.96 percent to win this game. Seattle is coming off a dominant defensive performance in Week 7, and it’s back at home where it is 3-1 so far in the 2026 season. However, the Bears have not lost a single game that Williams has started – and finished – this season. The Bears are an interesting team this season. A lot of their season-long offensive numbers are skewed a bit from the three games that Williams has missed, yet they’ve scored 30 or more points in every matchup that he’s been able to stay healthy in. Plus, Chicago is shockingly seventh in the league in success rate on defense despite allowing the most yards per play in the league. Oddsmakers are clearly buying the Seattle defense, which is No. 2 in EPA/Play, No. 2 in success rate and No. 1 in yards per play allowed – by a wide margin – this season. The Seahawks are allowing just 4.0 yards per play while the next-best team (Minnesota) is allowing 4.5. After the Seahawks shut down Patrick Mahomes in Week 7, it seems like oddsmakers have the defending champs’ defense as the best unit in this Week 8 clash. There’s a chance this line moves as the week progresses, and fans can look forward to Ben Johnson and Mike Macdonald scheming against each other in a potential playoff preview. A win for either team will go a long way because of tiebreakers with the NFC West and North featuring seven viable playoff teams. Only five will be able to get in (since the winners of the NFC East and NFC South will clinch two of the seven playoff spots). Three of the four writers nailed their upset bets. Gilberto Manzano correctly predicted the Atlanta Falcons to upset the San Francisco 49ers, Mike Kadlick cashed in on the Miami Dolphins to upset the New York Jets, and yours truly was in on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to beat the Carolina Panthers. We move on to Week 8 hoping for another successful performance from our upset bets. Gilberto Manzano , NFL Staff Writer Iain MacMillan , Senior Editor, Betting Peter Dewey , Associate Managing Editor, Betting All odds listed are via DraftKings Sportsbook Gilberto Manzano Week 8 Upset Pick Miami Dolphins (+250) vs. New England Patriots After getting three consecutive upset picks correct, I need to heat check myself. There’s no better way to do that than taking the one-win Dolphins against Drake Maye and the Patriots. Surprisingly, I have plenty of reasons to like this bet. Divisional games are often close, and New England has a long history of struggling in Miami. Also, the Dolphins have plenty of confidence after beating the Jets last week, and this offense is a lot better with rookie wide receiver Caleb Douglas, who contributed two catches for 70 yards and two touchdowns in his first game since sustaining an ankle injury in Week 2. I’m playing with house money, and I’m putting it on the Dolphins. Peter Dewey Week 8 Upset Pick Atlanta Falcons (+114) vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers The Falcons may be the most confusing team in the NFL, but I think their best version is the top squad in the NFC South. I’m buying Atlanta as a road underdog against a Tampa Bay team that is 0-4 against the spread at home and potentially overvalued after a Week 7 rout of the Carolina Panthers. Baker Mayfield (thumb) wasn’t asked to do much, but the Bucs beat up a Carolina defense that has allowed the most yards per carry in the NFL. That won’t be the case against Atlanta, which is No. 4 in EPA/Rush and 12th in opponent yards per play in 2026. Tampa Bay has been great defensively as well (third in EPA/Play, seventh in yards per play), but the offensive upside is capped with Mayfield and Emeka Egbuka banged up. Plus, this Falcons offense has been much better with Michael Penix Jr. under center over the last few weeks. The Falcons are 3-2 when Penix starts, and I love this price against a Tampa Bay team with clear flaws and a quarterback at less than 100 percent. Iain MacMillan Week 8 Upset Pick Chicago Bears (+140) vs. Seattle Seahawks I'm ready to believe in the Chicago Bears. Ben Johnson is clearly the real deal as head coach, and Caleb Williams has improved significantly since last season. Last season, he ranked 39th out of 45 starting quarterbacks in completion percentage over expected. This season, he ranks first at +9.0%. The Bears' defense has also been better than people expected this season, ranking fourth in the NFL in opponent success rate. I still have some concerns surrounding the Seattle offense. It did enough to beat the Chiefs last week, but their running game is still weak, and Sam Darnold hasn't been as efficient as he was a year ago. I'll take the Bears as my upset pick of the week. The NFL Week 8 finale is a big one: the Chicago Bears visit the defending-champion Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football. Both teams are coming off statement non-conference wins, and my early Bears vs. Seahawks predictions pick through what could very well be a postseason preview in the NFC. Early Bears vs Seahawks spread pick: Bears +3.5 Much like the Seattle Seahawks benefited from a mini bye after a Thursday night game, the Chicago Bears get a few bonus days to rest and prep for this massive Monday matchup. Chicago, which beat New England on TNF in Week 7, could have running back Kyle Monangai in action, which gives Ben Johnson one of his best offensive weapons. This Bears attack is rolling with QB Caleb Williams another week healthier from his hamstring pull. Johnson had success against Mike Macdonald's defense in 2024 with Detroit, averaging 7.8 yards per play and going a perfect 5-for-5 in the red zone in a win over the Seahawks. Granted, Seattle was missing multiple defensive starters for that showdown. Key bodies on Chicago's defense are also trending toward playing in Week 8. The Bears are a dangerous stop unit, creating chaos with a blitz-heavy pass rush. Chicago, which sits fourth in pressure rate, has generated 19 sacks and 10 takeaways. Seattle QB Sam Darnold has suffered through the highest rate of pressure per dropback to start 2026 and just lost his LT Charles Cross to an ankle injury. Darnold's PFF ratings tank when under duress, including four of his eight interceptions coming vs. pressure. Dybantsa delivers in debut Bears vs. Seahawks bold predictions for Week 8 Monday Night Football Steve Silverman, ClutchPoints Wed, October 28, 2026 at 11:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Chicago Bears have demonstrated quite a bit of explosiveness this season, especially when Caleb Williams is under center and running back Kyle Monangai is healthy and in the lineup. Williams has been in the lineup for the past two games and has demonstrated no ill effects from the hamstring injury that sidelined him earlier in the year. Monangai has missed the last three games and while he is improving, there are no guarantees that he will be back in the lineup for this game. The Seahawks have not been at their best in the first half of the season and they take a 4-3 record into this home game. They are coming off a key Sunday night victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in which their defense performed at a peak level. They will need that kind of effort against the Bears. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sam Darnold was one of the keys to Seattle's surge to last year's Super Bowl title. He has not been as efficient this season, as interceptions have been an issue. The Bears defense got a huge lift from their ability to create takeaways last year. They have not been as proficient in that area this season — minus-1 on the takeaway/turnover table — but they have been a middle-of-the-pack defense that has been moderately capable this season. This game could come down to turnover differential, and if the Bears are going to win on the road, they have to gain an advantage in this area. Williams will throw for 250 yards and 2 TDs Williams has demonstrated that he can rise to the occasion and handle pressure. He has an excellent partnership with head coach Ben Johnson, and it appears that those two will allow the Bears to remain contenders in the division and the NFC for several years. Williams has all the tools that an outstanding quarterback needs, and as the No. 1 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, nearly all scouts and personnel specialists were predicting great things for him. However, Williams struggled in his rookie season under former head coach Matt Eberflus. That coach did not have the wherewithal to teach and demand outstanding play from Williams. However that changed under Johnson, and the quarterback reads and understands defenses, and he knows how to pick apart good defenses and make key plays. The one area that scouts did not get right about Williams was his speed and escapability from the pocket. He was thought to be above average or good in that area, and that assessment did not give him enough credit. He is sensational in that area. He has a strong partnership with wide receivers Rome Odunze and Luther Burden, as well as big-play tight end Colston Loveland. This trio should be able to cause problems for the Seattle defense, which is one of the strongest units in the league. Williams and the receivers will not overpower the Seahawks defense, but the quarterback will throw 2 TD passes and approach the 275-yard mark. Smith-Njigba is unstoppable, will exceed 125 yards and score a TD Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Bears regularly have to contend with outstanding receivers like Justin Jefferson, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Christian Watson in the NFC North. However, Seattle wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba is at another level. He is coming off a sensational game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Smith-Njigba was targeted 12 times by Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold and he caught 9 passes for 150 yards and 1 touchdown. The Chiefs knew he was the central point of the Seattle offensive game plan, yet defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo could not do anything to slow him down. Stopping him was out of the question. Chicago defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will face the same issue. Allen certainly knows what it is like to face outstanding wideouts in the NFC North, but Smith-Njigba may be too strong for the Bears defense. He has caught 58 passes for 867 yards and 8 TDs, and asking CBs Jaylon Johnson, Malik Muhammad and Kyler Gordon to prevent him from making big plays will be folly. The best way for the Bears to go about it would be pressuring Darnold and keep him from delivering accurate passes. The Bears have registered 19 sacks and Darnold has been trapped 14 times thus far. Allen's top priority will be to make sure his personnel gets in Darnold's face and prevents him from getting the ball to Smith-Njigba. That scenario is unlikely, but it is Chicago's best defensive hope. Bold game prediction: Seahawks 27, Bears 24 The Bears have the weapons to go into Seattle and give the defending champions a battle for 60 minutes. This is the kind of game that Johnson and Williams would like to use as a measuring stick. However, the Seahawks have already lost 3 games and they can't afford to lose any more. They will have a major challenge chasing down the 49ers in the NFC West, and dropping a home game to a solid team is not in their plans. The Seahawks played their best all-around game against the Chiefs in Week 7, and they will stay on track against the Bears. Seattle wins a close, well-played game against Williams and the Bears. Seattle will need contributions from its top playmakers and another sweltering performance from its defense to give the team its best shot to secure a statement victory against Chicago. Here are three bold predictions for the primetime showdown slated for this coming Monday night. Seahawks will limit Caleb Williams to his worst performance of the season Bears quarterback Caleb Williams enters the matchup with 1,020 passing yards, five touchdowns and one interception, completing 71.0% of his passes this season. However, Seattle's defense will make life difficult for Williams, limiting his opportunities down the field and taking away his ability to be as dynamic as usual when scrambling out of the pocket. Williams will finish with season lows in completion percentage, passing yards and passing touchdowns thanks to Seattle's unit disrupting his rhythm. Seattle will be aggressive in attacking underneath and using Barner as a reliable target in key situations. Barner will ultimately record over 70 receiving yards and a receiving touchdown in the game. Seahawks reserve makes a big difference in win Seattle's depth will become a major factor as the game unfolds. Tyrice Knight will provide an important spark for the Seahawks with timely defensive stops, physical play and special-teams contributions. Knight himself will go for a sack, quarterback hit and tackle for loss in what will be his biggest game of the year. His impact will swing momentum in Seattle's favor and help the Seahawks take Williams out of his comfort zone and ultimately come away with a win in a hard-fought contest. away.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams slapped with another big NFL punishment
away.blurb: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is back on the field after being out for three games with an injury, but he's already getting slapped with punishment from the NFL. According to a report from NBC Sports' Pro Football Talk , the NFL has officially fined Chicago's quarterback $23,882 for wearing an "unauthorized logo" on his shoes during the Week 7 game against the New England Patriots . That's two times the amount he was fined last week for wearing the shoes in Week 6, which was $11,941. But it appears Williams isn't sweating it. This week, he said that he'll still sport the shoes, which don't have an official deal with the NFL. Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams isn't backing down after another NFL fine "I try to be healthy. They're smart cleats," Williams said during a presser this week, per NBC Sports. "They're science cleats, and they've been working for me. A bunch of other guys wear them in the league, and they're forward-focused on making sure players stay on the field, and that's what I'm always focused on." Mike Florio says Williams "presumably will appeal the second fine." Plus, the NFL is expected to keep giving fines to Williams in increasing amounts until Williams gives in, Florio notes. "At some point, the league could (in theory) prevent Williams from playing in the non-conforming shoes," he adds. "Neither fine letter, however, warns him that he could be kept from playing with the Caddix shoes." Next up for the Bears, Williams and his cleats will take on the Seattle Seahawks for a "Monday Night Football" matchup on the road. Want more articles like this? away.headline: Kyle Monangai gets optimistic injury update before Bears-Seahawks clash
away.blurb: Kyle Monangai inching closer to Bears return The Chicago Bears have been without Kyle Monangai for their last three games due to a turf toe injury. While the franchise has gone 2-1 in that span, the running back’s absence has been made painfully clear. In the four games he appeared in prior to his injury, Monangai turned 60 carries into 324 yards and three touchdowns. He picked up his injury after rushing 30 times for 146 yards and two touchdowns against the New York Jets. While his total rushing attempts skews the metric a tad, Monangai’s 5.4 yards per carry ranks third-best in the NFL. Head coach Ben Johnson loves to run the ball. And the former seventh-round pick has proven he can be a consistent force in the offense. Johnson undoubtedly wants Monangai back on the field as soon as possible. That reality is becoming increasingly likely as the Week 8 Seattle Seahawks clash looms. The Bears are set to release their first injury report of the week on Thursday. How Monangai is listed will be telling of his Week 8 status. But he seems more likely to suit up than he has in past weeks, via Jeremy Fowler of ESPN. “Bears running back Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has missed the past three weeks, but his chances are better of playing this week,” Fowler wrote. The injury bug has bitten the Bears heavily on both sides of the ball in 2026. They’ve managed to battle through, holding a 5-2 record heading into Monday Night Football. Still, Chicago is hoping to have a cleaner bill of health as the season progresses. In terms of Monangai, the franchise will continue to be cautious with his recovery. Still, the fact he wasn’t placed on injured reserve was a sign Chicago didn’t expect him to miss four or more games. If he is able to practice, and his body responds accordingly, the Bears may have their bowling ball in the backfield against the Seahawks. Want more articles like this? home.headline: Seahawks Give New Zach Charbonnet Injury Update Before Bears Game
home.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks are getting closer to Zach Charbonnet's return, but head coach Mike Macdonald isn't ready to put a date on it. "He had a great week, great spirits," Macdonald said. "We have to remember, it's going to be nine months out of ACL surgery. How many people have ever done that? What's it like, Adrian Peterson?" Macdonald wasn't predicting a similar season for Charbonnet. Rather, his comments underscored the significance of attempting to return from major knee surgery on such an accelerated timeline. The roster move made him eligible to play, but Macdonald has repeatedly emphasized that his return will depend on the team's recovery plan. Charbonnet's eventual return would give Seattle another proven rushing option, particularly near the goal line. His absence has been especially noticeable with Kenneth Walker III now playing for the Chiefs and rookie Jadarian Price sidelined. Rookie Jadarian Price is expected to return to practice this week after missing multiple games with a chest injury. He went on to rush for 2,097 yards and win NFL MVP honors.
